# Proverbs 22 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A good reputation is worth more than enormous wealth, and being respected is better than having silver and gold.

**2** Rich and poor have this in common — the LORD made them both.

**3** A perceptive person sees danger coming and takes cover, but the naive walk straight into it and pay the price.

**4** True humility and respect for the LORD lead to wealth, honor, and life.

**5** The path of the crooked is full of traps and thorns. If you value your life, stay far away.

**6** Start children on the right path, and even when they're old they'll stay on it.

**7** The rich rule over the poor, and anyone who borrows becomes a servant to the lender.

**8** If you plant injustice, you'll harvest disaster, and the power you used to bully people will eventually fail.

**9** Generous people will be blessed, because they share what they have with those in need.

**10** Get rid of the mocker and the fighting stops — the quarreling and insults disappear with them.

**11** If you value a pure heart and speak with grace, even the king will be your friend.

**12** The LORD watches over what is true, but He demolishes the plans of the dishonest.

**13** The lazy person says, 'There's a lion out there! I'll be killed if I go outside!' — any excuse to avoid work.

**14** The seductive words of the unfaithful are a deep trap — those under God's judgment fall right in.

**15** Foolishness is woven into a child's nature, but firm discipline can pull it out.

**16** Taking advantage of the poor to get richer, or giving gifts to the wealthy — both lead to poverty.

**17** Listen carefully to what wise people say, and take what I'm teaching to heart,

**18** Because keeping this wisdom inside you is a beautiful thing — have it ready on your lips whenever you need it.

**19** I'm telling you all this today so that your confidence will be in the LORD — yes, you personally.

**20** Haven't I written out thirty sayings for you — full of sound advice and solid knowledge?

**21** So you can recognize what's true and reliable, and give honest answers to anyone who asks.

**22** Don't exploit poor people just because they can't fight back, and don't crush vulnerable people in court,

**23** Because the LORD Himself will take up their case and will destroy anyone who destroys them.

**24** Don't make friends with someone who's always angry, and don't spend time with hotheads,

**25** Or you'll pick up their habits and set a trap for yourself.

**26** Don't be the kind of person who co-signs loans or guarantees other people's debts.

**27** If you can't pay, they'll take your bed right out from under you.

**28** Don't move ancient boundary markers that previous generations put in place.

**29** Have you seen someone truly excellent at their craft? They'll end up working for kings, not nobodies.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **22:2**: Simple but revolutionary — rich and poor are equally God's creation. Economic status is not an indicator of divine favor or disfavor.

- **22:6**: One of the most famous — and most misapplied — verses in the Bible. It's an observation about tendencies, not a promise with a money-back guarantee.

- **22:22-23**: Powerful justice passage — don't exploit the vulnerable, because God will personally intervene as their attorney. He'll do to their oppressors what their oppressors did to them.

— PNEUMA
